## Landed: Gerrit change 1626 (merged)

`s3_doctor._git` now routes through `gitutil.run_git_write`, so the doctor inherits the
per-store advisory git-op lock, the bounded index/ref-lock retry and the transient read-fault
retry from the ONE implementation. The existing transient wrapper gained a single scoped marker
for the proven missing-object signature; no new retry loop, backoff policy or module was added.
`run_git_write` gained an optional timeout so the doctor keeps its own `_GIT_TIMEOUT` watchdog.
A bundle failure that survives the retries now reports an object-DB read failure instead of
sending the operator to `rebar fsck-recover` for a merge that never conflicted.

### Verification

The fault is injected at the PROCESS boundary (a `PATH` git shim), not by patching a rebar
internal, so the tests pin observable behaviour and were honest RED: before the change the
transient test failed with the exact CI text (`could not bundle merged tip … fatal: bad object
HEAD`) and the persistent-fault test recorded exactly ONE bundle attempt, proving no retry
existed. After: first attempt fails, identical retry succeeds, heal completes losslessly. A
non-transient failure is still raised on the first attempt, so the marker cannot mask a real
error.

On the landed tree: 27 s3_doctor/doctor tests pass, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`
green; CI voted `Verified +1` and the review bot `LLM-Review +1`.

### Closing class: flaky

The three CI failures were a nondeterministic runner-side object-DB read transient — the trigger
was never reproduced locally (0 failures in 27 runs) and remains unproven. What was proven and
fixed is the structural gap that made the transient fatal here and harmless everywhere else.
